title: Open the early pull request right after the candidate commit
summary: Move the early push and pull request call so it runs as soon as the producer's candidate is committed, ahead of admission and Athena's own checks. That way CI overlaps the checks and the verifier instead of starting about 12 minutes later. The merge stays gated on verification and athena land. The audience is the maintainer, who wants the landing commit to find a cached CI pass.

defaults_applied.how: Fake-host tests cover ordering and the never-merged-on-failure case. Clippy and fmt are clean.
Criteria check call order and the absence of a merge on the fake host, not that the wiring exists.
The CHANGELOG landing time is labeled measured or estimate.
The fix moves the call to the earliest point after the candidate commit.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: In run.rs early_pr is called after admission and fingerprinting, and a candidate that fails admission returns before it. The fix is to call it right after the candidate commit is made, before admission and the checks. Repository reading found the call at run.rs:1645, with the checks at about line 1700.
The existing test in run_pin_tests.rs is the natural home for the ordering test even though the request lists only run.rs, gh.rs and CHANGELOG.md.
The real landing time cannot be measured by the producer. The CHANGELOG records a placeholder or a note that it is to be recorded at the next real landing, and is not filled with a made-up number.
A failed candidate's pull request stays open for the retry, which force-updates the same branch. Closing it with the job is existing behavior and is left as is.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test using the fake host (run_pin_tests.rs, extending early_pr_pushes_the_candidate_and_opens_the_pull_request...) shows the push and open_pr calls happen after the candidate commit exists and before the first Athena check starts and before the verifier starts. Run: cargo test -p athena-core early_pr

A test shows that a candidate failing Athena's checks or rejected by the verifier produces no merge call on the fake host, and that its pull request is left for the retry or closed with the job. Run: cargo test -p athena-core
A failing early push or open still only yields the single warning line and the same job outcome. Run: cargo test -p athena-core a_failing_early_step

In run.rs the early_pr call sits directly after the candidate is committed, before the admission and check steps, with the comment updated to say so. gh.rs changes only if the early-PR helper needs it.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry for this change. It says the landing time of the next real landing is to be recorded there as measured and labels any number not yet measured as an estimate. It does not invent a measured landing time.
cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean and cargo test passes.

out_of_scope: Changing how athena land waits for CI or merges
Changing which checks Athena runs or their duration
Changes to CI workflow files, athena.toml or defaults.toml
departures: The CHANGELOG criterion needs a measured landing time that exists only after a real landing, which lowers verification odds a little.
urgent_reason: Cuts about 12 minutes of wasted time per landing: the landing commit's CI run finds no cached pass and redoes the full 16-minute run.
